description_for_human: Search and read entities, officers and the records held on them in Kube.
description_for_model: Read-only access to the user's Kube corporate-registry and entity-management data over the Model Context Protocol. Use it whenever the user asks about legal entities or officers/directors, and for any of the records held on them: an entity's or officer's appointments, roles, contacts, addresses, alternates and user defined fields; an entity's compliance dates, meetings, registrations and activities; an officer's committees and external appointments; and the activity workload owned by the signed-in user or their teams, across every entity they can see. Provides search across entities and officers, detailed lookups for a given entity or officer, and field catalogues that map this instance's own UI labels to stable field keys. Every result is scoped to the signed-in user's Kube permissions and field-level redaction; it cannot create, change, or delete data.

tools.name: search_parties
tools.description:
PRIMARY search across Entities (companies, LLPs, trusts, etc.) AND Officers (directors, secretaries, PSCs)
in a single call, filtered to records the signed-in user can see. Use this FIRST when you are not sure
whether the user means an entity or an officer, or to quickly find a party by name — it mirrors the Kube
global search box.

Returns very cut-down rows to keep context small:
- `KubeRef` — stable id, prefixed `E|` for entities or `O|` for officers.
- `Type` — `Entity` or `Officer`.
- `Name`, `Active` — display name; whether active in Kube.
- `Registrars` — the registrar(s) this party is recorded under (the registrar for an entity, a comma-joined list for an officer); a short line to help tell same-named hits apart.

`query` matches entity and officer names (AND across whitespace words) — and, for entities, also
IDENTIFIERS: the registrar-issued entity/registration number, the Kube company code, and a pasted
E|/O|-prefixed KubeRef. A pasted company number like `09876543` resolves in this one call — do not
report "not found" for an identifier without trying it here first. Strip company suffixes (Ltd,
Limited, PLC, LLP, Inc, Corp, GmbH, S.A., Pty, etc.) from entity names — they reduce recall. Officer
records do not store personal titles / honorifics (Mr, Mrs, Dr, Sir, etc.), so omit them when searching
for a person; but such words can be a genuine part of a company name (e.g. 'Dr. Martens', 'Mr Kipling'),
so keep them when the target may be a company, and retry with the original term included if a search
returns nothing. Results are ranked by relevance, scored over a capped candidate set per party type — so
`TotalItems` can exceed the rows paging can return; if you hit an empty page before reaching `TotalItems`,
narrow `query` instead of paging further. For full entity detail, follow up with `get_entity`
using an `E|` KubeRef.

Paged: `Items` is one page; `TotalItems` is the total match count.
A pure count ("how many …") needs only `TotalItems` from page 1.
For the complete set (summary, aggregate, comparison, anything over "all"), page with `pageSize` 100 (the max), incrementing `page`, until you have all `TotalItems` items BEFORE answering — one page is not a sufficient basis.
When `TotalItems` is large, prefer narrowing with the filter parameters; page everything only when the complete set is genuinely required.

query.description: Name or identifier to search for; words are AND-ed. Matches entity and officer names, entity/registration numbers, company codes, and pasted KubeRefs.

active.description: true (default) = active parties only; false = also include inactive parties. OMIT this parameter for the normal case. Send `false` only when the user has specifically asked about inactive records.

pageSize.description: Default 25, max 100. Use 100 when retrieving the full result set.

tools.name: search_entities
tools.description:
Search Entity records (companies, LLPs, trusts, etc.) in this Kube instance.
Results are server-side filtered to records the signed-in user can see — no client-side filtering needed.

Search tips:
- `query` matches names — current name, previous names, and trading names. All words must match — `Acme Holdings` requires both.
- Strip company suffixes (Ltd, Limited, PLC, LLP, Inc, Corp, GmbH, S.A., Pty, etc.) from `query` — they are stripped from the indexed data, so including them reduces recall.
- Everything that is not a name has its own parameter: registrar, registrar country, entity type, classification, jurisdiction, SIC code, business unit, division, entity group, registrar status, company status, responsible owner, tags, audit status, client name, client number. Non-name terms in `query` return zero results.
- Every filter parameter takes a LIST. Values within one parameter are OR-ed, and the parameters are AND-ed: `entityType: ["LLP", "Private Limited Company"]` with `jurisdiction: ["England and Wales"]` means LLPs or private limited companies, in England and Wales.
- Every filter matches on SUBSTRING, case-insensitive, except `companyStatus` and `auditStatus`, which take one of a fixed set of values and name the valid ones if you get it wrong.
- A filter you are not permitted to use is REFUSED, not ignored: the error names the parameter, and retrying without it is the fix.

Result fields (optional fields may be absent; null fields are omitted from JSON):
- `KubeRef` — stable cross-instance id, prefixed `E|` (e.g. `E|6FE4BF`).
- `Name`, `Active` — current registered name; whether active in Kube.
- `CompanyCode` — short code shown alongside the name in Kube UI.
- `EntityNumber` — the registrar-issued entity/registration number (answer listing
  questions like "our companies with their company numbers" straight from these rows,
  no per-entity fetch needed).
- `Registrar`, `RegistrarCountry`, `Jurisdiction` — e.g. `Companies House`, `United Kingdom`, `South Africa`.
- `Status` — the entity's status in Kube, e.g. `Active`, `InactiveClosed`. This is what `companyStatus` filters, NOT the registrar's own status, which `registrarStatus` filters and which is not returned here.
- `EntityType` — e.g. `Private Limited Company`, `LLP`.
- `RedactedProperties` — names of fields withheld on that record; absent when nothing is withheld.

Withheld vs not-recorded: a field is null/absent either because no value is recorded, or because it was withheld. Distinguish them via `RedactedProperties` — a field named there was withheld and may well hold a value, for any of several reasons this connector does not report and you should not guess at; a null field NOT listed there simply has no recorded value.

Classification, business unit, division, entity group, SIC code, registrar status, responsible owner, tags, audit status and client name/number are filterable but not returned per-result — read them off get_entity.

Paged: `Items` is one page; `TotalItems` is the total match count.
A pure count ("how many …") needs only `TotalItems` from page 1.
For the complete set (summary, aggregate, comparison, anything over "all"), page with `pageSize` 100 (the max), incrementing `page`, until you have all `TotalItems` items BEFORE answering — one page is not a sufficient basis.
When `TotalItems` is large, prefer narrowing with the filter parameters; page everything only when the complete set is genuinely required.

query.description: Name search; AND across whitespace tokens. Omit for all visible entities.

active.description: true (default) = active entities only; false = also include inactive entities. OMIT this parameter for the normal case. Send `false` only when the user has specifically asked about inactive records.

pageSize.description: Default 10, max 100. Use 100 when retrieving the full result set.

registrarCountry.description: Registrar's country: full name (substring, e.g. 'United Kingdom') or ISO Alpha-2/3 code (exact, e.g. 'GB', 'GBR').

registrar.description: Registrar (substring). Either the bare name ('Companies House') or the 'Name [Country]' form the Kube dropdown shows.

registrarStatus.description: The registrar's own status for the entity, as the registrar words it (e.g. 'Active', 'Dissolved'); substring. Distinct from `companyStatus`, which is the entity's status inside Kube.

companyStatus.description: The entity's status inside Kube: 'Active', 'Inactive - closed', 'Inactive - sold', 'Inactive - pending', 'Inactive - closed and merged', 'Preparing for incorporation', 'Ready for incorporation', 'Processing Incorporation'. AND-ed with `active`, so an inactive status needs `active: false` too.

responsibleOwner.description: Responsible owner, by display name or email address; substring. Never a user id.

tags.description: Tags on the entity; substring on the tag's name. An entity matches if it carries any of them.

clientName.description: Client name; substring. Matches the entity's CURRENT client only, not one it used to belong to.

clientNumber.description: Client number; substring. Matches the entity's CURRENT client only, not one it used to belong to.

tools.name: get_entity
tools.description:
Get full detail for a single Entity by its KubeRef (E|-prefixed, e.g. E|6FE4BF), filtered to what the
signed-in user may see.

Returns the Profile fields by default: KubeRef, Name, Active, EntityNumber, BusinessNumber, Status,
EntityType, Registrar, Country, Jurisdiction, Classification, EntityGroup, BusinessUnit, Division,
EmailAddress, IncorporatedOn, CessationDate, LastSoldOn, RegistrarStatus, GoverningLaw, ParentCompany,
ParentCompanyNumber, ParentCompanyKubeRef, RegisteredOfficeAddress, CorrespondenceAddress,
RegisteredInspectionAddress, Tags, NatureOfBusiness (NAICS/SIC codes — Code + Description),
PreviousNames (Name + period), TradingNames.

Parent company is the one recorded on the entity's Profile tab (name and/or registry number).
ParentCompany is the linked entity's name when the number matches an entity you may see — in which case
ParentCompanyKubeRef is its KubeRef, usable with this tool — otherwise the free-text name as recorded.
A parent recorded only under Relationships is a separate corporate-relationship record and is not
returned here.

Other parts of an entity's record have their own tools: get_entity_appointments (officer appointments),
get_entity_dates (compliance dates), get_entity_roles (service-role appointments such as auditor),
get_entity_contacts (contact records), get_entity_addresses (address book), get_entity_meetings
(meetings the entity held, as minuted), get_entity_registrations (branch, foreign and tax-only
registered presences), get_entity_activities (tracked tasks and filings with due dates),
get_entity_alternates (appointments held by an alternate) and get_entity_udfs (user defined field
values).

Set `fetchAdditionalDetails` = true to also return the Details fields: EntityCode, LeiNumber, Overview,
BusinessActivity, BusinessReportingGroup, ApiConnection, RiskFactors, CountryCode, ResponsibleOwner,
AcquisitionDate, AccessCategories. When false they are omitted — ignore them.

Withheld vs not-recorded: a field is null/absent either because no value is recorded, or because it was
withheld. `RedactedProperties` lists the names of the fields that were withheld — each may well hold a
value, for any of several reasons this connector does not report and you should not guess at, so do not
tell the user they lack a permission. A null field NOT listed there simply has no recorded value.

fetchAdditionalDetails.description: true to also return the additional Details-tab fields; default false.

tools.name: get_entity_appointments
tools.description:
List the officer appointments on an entity (directors, secretaries, etc.) — Entity > People > Appointments.
Read-only and filtered to what the signed-in user may see.

For role questions ("who are the directors of X?"), filter server-side with `isDirector: true` (semantic
flag, robust to renamed appointment types) or `appointmentType` (exact type name) — that keeps the answer
complete beyond one page instead of scanning mixed rows.

`query` matches this entity's own name and the appointee's forenames and surname — the same two columns the
tab's keyword box searches; AND across whitespace tokens, substring, case-insensitive. It does not match
AppointmentType or any date.

Per appointment: Name (appointee), EntityKubeRef (E| — this entity) and OfficerKubeRef (O| — the appointee,
follow up with get_officer), IsOfficerAccessible, OfficerAppointmentId (stable appointment id), AppointmentType,
IsDirector, AppointmentGrouping, AppointedOn, ResignedOn.

A row may name an appointee you cannot open. It is still listed, matching how Kube shows that appointee as
plain text rather than a link: the row keeps its Name but has NO OfficerKubeRef, carries
IsOfficerAccessible: false, and names OfficerKubeRef, nulled, in its RedactedProperties. Such a row cannot be
followed up with get_officer, and this tool returns nothing else about that appointee.
IsOfficerAccessible is true for an appointee you can open.

Paged: Items plus Page, PageSize, TotalItems. Withheld date fields are nulled and named in each row's
RedactedProperties. Returns an empty page when this section is not returned to you on this entity, and
equally when the entity simply has no appointments — a withheld section says so explicitly, so a bare empty
page means nothing is recorded.

Inactive rows are EXCLUDED BY DEFAULT, matching the ticked active-only checkbox on the Kube tab this
reflects. `TotalItems` therefore counts active rows only, and is NOT how many exist on the record.
So do not present a default-filtered count as a total ("this entity has 4 registrations") — either say the
count is of active rows, or re-query for the rest. The filter parameter's own description says how.
Leave `active` unset for that default; send it only to ask for the inactive rows as well.

Paged: `Items` is one page; `TotalItems` is the total match count.
A pure count ("how many …") needs only `TotalItems` from page 1.
For the complete set (summary, aggregate, comparison, anything over "all"), page with `pageSize` 100 (the max), incrementing `page`, until you have all `TotalItems` items BEFORE answering — one page is not a sufficient basis.
When `TotalItems` is large, prefer narrowing with the filter parameters; page everything only when the complete set is genuinely required.

active.description: true (default) = active appointments only, matching the tab's ticked active-only checkbox; false = also include resigned ones. EmailAddress, Address (the contact's own address, as a single line).

whitespace tokens, substring, case-insensitive.

CountyRegion, Postcode, Country, plus EffectiveFrom (the date the address takes effect, when recorded).

when this section is not returned to you on this entity, and equally when the entity simply has no

tools.name: get_entity_registrations

List an entity's registrations — Entity > Registrations. Read-only and filtered to what the signed-in user
may see.

A registration is a registered presence this entity holds in a jurisdiction — a branch, a foreign
registration or a tax-only registration — held in Kube as a child record of the entity with its own
registrar, registration number, status and address. These are NOT the entity's own profile: for the
entity's own name, number, registrar and status use get_entity. Nor are they other entities: a registration
belongs to this entity and has no separate entity record.

Per registration: KubeRef (R|-prefixed — it identifies this registration row and is NOT accepted by
get_entity), Name, Country, Jurisdiction, Registrar, RegistrationNumber, RegisteredDate,

tools.name: get_entity_activities
tools.description:
List the activities recorded against an entity — Entity > Activities. Read-only and filtered to what the
signed-in user may see.

An activity is a piece of work tracked in Kube: a task or a statutory filing, with an owner, a team, a due
date and a done/not-done state. These are NOT the entity's statutory compliance dates — for those (annual
return due, accounts made up to, and the other recurring deadlines on the entity's Dates tab) use
get_entity_dates. The distinction is that an activity is assignable work someone completes, while a
compliance date is a deadline the entity carries whether or not any work has been logged against it. Use
this tool for "what is outstanding / who is doing it / what is overdue"; use get_entity_dates for "when is
X due".

Results span the entity AND its registrations, matching the entity's Activities tab — an activity recorded
against a registration is included here, so do NOT also call this per registration or you will double-count.
Registrations carry their own access permissions, so only activities of registrations you can see are
included. Set `entityOnly: true` to restrict to the entity's own activities and exclude its registrations —
the tab itself has no equivalent toggle.

Every activity on the entity is returned whoever owns it. When the question is about the caller's OWN
workload rather than a named company's activities ("my confirmation statements", "what's outstanding for
me?"), use get_my_activities — that one covers only what the user or their teams own, spans every entity
they can see, and is the one whose ActivityId feeds the guided confirmation-statement completion.

Per activity: Activity (its name), Category (e.g. 'Filing', 'Compliance'), Type, DueOn, IsComplete, Team, Owner
(the responsible user's display name, or 'KAIA' for an activity KAIA owns), plus PartyName and EntityKubeRef.
Type is the filing type for a statutory filing and the activity type for anything else — whichever the activity
carries, matching the single Type column Kube shows.

PartyName and EntityKubeRef identify the party the activity actually belongs to, which is NOT always the entity
you queried: for an activity recorded against one of its registrations they are the registration's name and its
`R|` ref. An `R|` ref is not accepted by get_entity — match it against the KubeRef values from
get_entity_registrations on the same entity to identify which registration it is. Where the activity's party is
an officer or an external party rather than an entity, PartyName is that party's name and EntityKubeRef is
absent.

prefer them over paging through everything and filtering yourself:
- `active` — true (the DEFAULT) = active only, matching the tab's ticked active-only checkbox, which counts a
  completed activity as inactive; false also includes the completed ones.
- `isComplete` — the grid's separate Complete filter: true = completed only, false = outstanding only, omitted
  = no completion filter. It AND-s with `active`, so asking for completed work needs `active: false` too.
- `activityCategory` / `activityType` — category and type names as configured in this instance (substring);
  any one matches. Read the values off returned rows rather than guessing; a name that does not exist yields an
  empty page rather than an error. Both match the same values a row returns, so a filing type name works for
  `activityType`, and 'Filing' works for `activityCategory` — it selects the filings that read 'Filing'
  because they carry a filing type rather than a configured category.
- `dueOnOrAfter` / `dueOnOrBefore` — inclusive bounds on DueOn. Combine both for a window ('open filings
  due this quarter' is `complete: false` plus the two bounds). An activity with no recorded due date is
  excluded by either bound.
- `team` — team name (substring); any one matches. Omit for every team.
- `party` — party name (substring); any one matches. Matches the same value the row reports as PartyName, so a
  registration's activity is matched against the registration's name, not the entity's.
- `isOverdue` — true = past due and not yet complete only; false = everything else; omit for no filter on this.
- `filingReference` — filing reference (substring); any one matches. Only ever set on a statutory filing, so
  an activity that is not one cannot match.
- `filingPreparedOnOrAfter` / `filingPreparedOnOrBefore` — inclusive bounds on a statutory filing's prepared
  date. An activity with no recorded prepared date is excluded by either bound.
- `filingSubmittedOnOrAfter` / `filingSubmittedOnOrBefore` — inclusive bounds on a statutory filing's
  submitted date. An activity with no recorded submitted date is excluded by either bound.
- All four of those, and `dueOnOrAfter` / `dueOnOrBefore`, are DATES, not date-times — send 'YYYY-MM-DD'.
  The whole of a bounding day is included at both ends.

TotalItems — TotalItems counts the rows matching your filters, not the entity's whole activity list.
Returns an empty page when you may see the entity but lack permission to view its activity data, and equally
when the entity simply has no activities recorded, or none matching your filters — a withheld section says so
explicitly, so a bare empty page means nothing is recorded. An activity may name several parties, and it is
withheld entirely when the first of them is a party you cannot access, even where this entity is one of the
others.

reflects. `TotalItems` therefore counts active rows only, and is NOT how many exist on the record.
So do not present a default-filtered count as a total ("this entity has 4 registrations") — either say the
count is of active rows, or re-query for the rest. The filter parameter's own description says how.
Leave `active` unset for that default; send it only to ask for the inactive rows as well.

Paged: `Items` is one page; `TotalItems` is the total match count.
A pure count ("how many …") needs only `TotalItems` from page 1.
For the complete set (summary, aggregate, comparison, anything over "all"), page with `pageSize` 100 (the max), incrementing `page`, until you have all `TotalItems` items BEFORE answering — one page is not a sufficient basis.
When `TotalItems` is large, prefer narrowing with the filter parameters; page everything only when the complete set is genuinely required.

OMIT this parameter for the normal case. Send `false` only when the user has specifically asked about inactive records.

AND-ed with `active`, so completed activities need `active: false, isComplete: true` — `active` alone already excludes them. Same meaning as isComplete on get_my_activities.

tools.name: get_entity_alternates
tools.description:
List the appointments at an entity that are held by an alternate — Entity > People > Alternates. Read-only and
filtered to what the signed-in user may see.

An alternate stands in for one or more other appointees at the same entity, the principals. Each row here is
the ALTERNATE's own appointment, and `AlternateFor` names the principals that appointment stands in for. This
is a subset of get_entity_appointments, which lists every appointment at the entity: use that tool for "who
holds office at X" and this one for "who is an alternate at X, and for whom".

Per row: Name (the alternate), EntityKubeRef (E| — this entity), IsEntityAccessible (true: it is the entity you
asked about) and OfficerKubeRef (O| — the alternate, follow up with get_officer), OfficerAppointmentId,
AppointmentType, IsDirector, AppointmentGrouping, AppointedOn,
ResignedOn, IdentifierCode, CorrespondenceAddress, ResidentialAddress, Nationality, Occupation,
CountryOfResidency, DirectorshipType, DirectorshipStarted, DirectorshipLastRenewed, Notes — every one of these
describes the ALTERNATE's own appointment.

`AlternateFor` is a list, one entry per principal: Name, OfficerKubeRef (O|), IsOfficerAccessible,
AppointmentStart, AppointmentEnd, ResignationNotes.

Two different date pairs, and they are easy to confuse — read this before answering a date question.
AppointedOn / ResignedOn on the row are when the ALTERNATE's own appointment at the entity started and ended.
AlternateFor[].AppointmentStart / AppointmentEnd are when the LINK to that one principal started and ended —
the period the alternate stood in for that person. They are independent: an alternate can hold one
appointment while standing in for three principals over three different periods, and a link can end while
the appointment continues.

`active` filters the alternate's OWN appointment (the row's ResignedOn), not any link: true, the DEFAULT, returns
only appointments that are not resigned; false returns those alongside the ended ones. There is no
resigned-only setting, because the tab's checkbox offers none.

rather than a link: the entry has a Name but NO OfficerKubeRef, carries IsOfficerAccessible: false, and
`AlternateFor[].OfficerKubeRef` is named in that row's RedactedProperties. Such a principal cannot be
followed up with get_officer — there is nothing to pass it. IsOfficerAccessible is true for a principal you can
open.

`query` matches this entity's own name and the ALTERNATE's forenames and surname — the same columns the
tab's keyword box searches, and NOT the principals named in AlternateFor; AND across whitespace tokens,
substring, case-insensitive.

Paged: Items plus Page, PageSize, TotalItems. Appointments held by an alternate whose officer profile is
outside your access are omitted entirely. Withheld columns are nulled and named in each row's
RedactedProperties; when the alternate-for block is withheld the whole `AlternateFor` list is absent and
named there instead. Returns an empty page when this section is not returned to you on this entity, and
equally when the entity simply has no alternates — a withheld section says so explicitly, so a bare empty page
means nothing is recorded.

reflects. `TotalItems` therefore counts active rows only, and is NOT how many exist on the record.
So do not present a default-filtered count as a total ("this entity has 4 registrations") — either say the
count is of active rows, or re-query for the rest. The filter parameter's own description says how.

When `TotalItems` is large, prefer narrowing with the filter parameters; page everything only when the complete set is genuinely required.

tools.name: get_entity_udfs
tools.description:
List the user defined field (UDF) values recorded against an entity — Entity > User defined fields.
Read-only and filtered to what the signed-in user may see.

UDFs are configured by each Kube customer, so their names and meanings differ from instance to instance and
there is no fixed set. NEVER assume a particular field exists or guess what one means from its name — read
the rows this tool returns and report them as they are.

A field that is absent from these rows may mean any of several things, and this tool CANNOT tell them apart:
no value has been recorded against the entity, the field is not configured for this entity at all, or you
lack the grant for that field's scope. So report an absent field as "not recorded, or not visible to you" —
never state that the entity has no such field.

Three scopes, matching Kube's three inner tabs:
- `Field` — a standalone field. One row.
- `Group` — a field inside a named group of related fields. One row per field, each carrying `Group`.
- `List` — a table. One row per CELL, each carrying `List`, the 0-based `Row` number and the column's `Name`.
  A 3-column list with 2 rows is therefore SIX rows, not two. Group on `List` AND `Row` together to
  reassemble a table row: `Row` restarts at 0 in every list, so grouping on `Row` alone merges cells that
  belong to different lists. List names are not guaranteed unique either.

Per row: Scope, Group, List, Row, Name (the configured field name), Value (the value as text, dates ISO
yyyy-MM-dd), DataType (the configured value type, e.g. Text, MultilineText, Date, Boolean, Integer,
Percentage, CustomDropdown). A row with no Value has nothing recorded.

`scope` accepts Field, Group or List, case-insensitive. Omit it to get all three scopes in one page, ordered
Scope, then List name, then Row, then field Name. Any other value is rejected as an error rather than
silently ignored.

A UDF can be retired by a Kube administrator after values have been recorded against it. `active` (default
true) hides those, matching the ticked active-only checkbox on the Field and Group tabs. List cells are never
hidden by it, because the List tab has no such checkbox.

`query` matches a DIFFERENT set of columns per scope, mirroring each tab's own keyword box exactly — a single
blanket description would be wrong for two of the three:
- `Field` — the field's own Name and Description. Does NOT match the recorded value.
- `Group` — the containing GROUP's Name and Description only. Does NOT match the member field's own Name, and
  does NOT match the recorded value.
- `List` — nothing. The List tab's box searches only the cell's rendered value, which cannot be matched
  server-side, so a List-scope row never matches a non-empty `query` — page the rows and read them instead.
AND across whitespace tokens, substring, case-insensitive, within whichever of the above a row's scope allows.

Paged: Items plus Page, PageSize, TotalItems. Each scope has its own permission, so a page can contain one
scope and not another. Returns an empty page when you may see the entity but lack permission to view its
user defined fields — and equally when the entity simply has none recorded, which is common. A withheld
section says so explicitly, so a bare empty page means nothing is recorded.

Paged: `Items` is one page; `TotalItems` is the total match count.
A pure count ("how many …") needs only `TotalItems` from page 1.
For the complete set (summary, aggregate, comparison, anything over "all"), page with `pageSize` 100 (the max), incrementing `page`, until you have all `TotalItems` items BEFORE answering — one page is not a sufficient basis.
When `TotalItems` is large, prefer narrowing with the filter parameters; page everything only when the complete set is genuinely required.

pageSize.description: Default 25, max 100. Use 100 when retrieving the full result set.

scope.description: Restrict to one scope: 'Field', 'Group' or 'List' (case-insensitive). Omit for all three.

active.description: true (default) = fields and groups still in use only, matching the tab's ticked active-only checkbox; false = also include values whose field or group definition has since been retired. Never affects List scope, which has no such checkbox. OMIT this parameter for the normal case. Send `false` only when the user has specifically asked about inactive records.

query.description: Free-text filter; AND across whitespace tokens; Contains, case-insensitive. Matches a different set of columns per scope: Field matches the field's Name and Description; Group matches the containing group's Name and Description only, not the member field's; List never matches, since only the cell value is searchable there and that cannot be matched server-side. Omit for every row.

tools.name: search_officers
tools.description:
Search Officer records (people and corporate officers holding positions such as director, secretary or
PSC) in this Kube instance — the MCP counterpart of the Officers grid. Results are server-side filtered
to records the signed-in user can see — no client-side filtering needed.

Prefer search_parties for a quick name lookup across entities AND officers; use search_officers when you
need the Officers-grid filters below (appointed entity, registrar, appointment type, nationality, …) or
an active-only officer listing.

Search tips:
- `query` matches officer names — forenames, surname and former names. All words must match — `Jane Smith` requires both.
- Do NOT include personal titles or honorifics (Mr, Mrs, Dr, Sir, etc.) in `query` — they are not part of
  the searchable name fields, so including them reduces recall.
- For appointed entity / registrar / country / appointment type / directorship type / nationality /
  business unit / division / entity group / classification, use the matching parameter below; non-name
  terms in `query` return zero results.
- Every filter parameter takes a LIST, matching the grid's multi-select dropdowns: values OR within one
  parameter, parameters AND across. `appointmentType: ["Director", "Secretary"]` finds either;
  adding `country: ["GB"]` narrows both to GB.
- Optional text filters are Contains, case-insensitive; `appointedEntity` takes E|-prefixed KubeRefs.
- Combined appointment filters match the SAME appointment: `appointedEntity` + `appointmentType`
  (and directorship type / country / business unit / division / entity group / classification) find
  officers holding THAT role at THAT entity — someone who is only Secretary at the entity but Director
  elsewhere does not match. Registrar and nationality are officer-profile filters, independent of
  appointments.

Result fields (one row per officer; null fields are omitted from JSON):
- `KubeRef` — stable officer id, prefixed `O|` (e.g. `O|E993B7`). Follow up with get_officer,
  get_officer_appointments or get_officer_roles.
- `Name` — display name as the Officers grid shows it: `SURNAME, Forenames (Title)`.
- `Nationality` — from the officer's preferred profile.
- `DateOfBirth` — from the officer's preferred profile; the standard disambiguator when several
  officers share a name.
- `RedactedProperties` — names of fields withheld on that record; absent when nothing is withheld. A field
  named there was withheld and may well hold a value, for any of several reasons this connector does not
  report and you should not guess at. A null field NOT listed there simply has no recorded value.

Paged: `Items` is one page; `TotalItems` is the total match count.
A pure count ("how many …") needs only `TotalItems` from page 1.
For the complete set (summary, aggregate, comparison, anything over "all"), page with `pageSize` 100 (the max), incrementing `page`, until you have all `TotalItems` items BEFORE answering — one page is not a sufficient basis.
When `TotalItems` is large, prefer narrowing with the filter parameters; page everything only when the complete set is genuinely required.

query.description: Name search; AND across whitespace tokens; matches forenames, surname and former names. Omit titles/honorifics. Omit for all visible officers.

active.description: true (default) = only officers with an active profile; false = also include inactive officers. OMIT this parameter for the normal case. Send `false` only when the user has specifically asked about inactive records.

pageSize.description: Default 10, max 100. Use 100 when retrieving the full result set.

appointedEntity.description: Appointed entity KubeRefs, each E|-prefixed (e.g. ['E|6FE4BF']) — officers appointed to ANY of them.

registrar.description: Registrar holding the officer's profile (substring). Either the bare name ('Companies House') or the 'Name [Country]' form the Kube dropdown shows.

country.description: Appointed entity's registrar countries: full name (substring, e.g. 'United Kingdom') or ISO Alpha-2/3 code (exact, e.g. 'GB', 'GBR').

tools.name: get_officer
tools.description:
Get detail for a single officer (person) by their KubeRef (O|-prefixed, e.g. O|E993B7), filtered to what
the signed-in user may see. Find an officer's KubeRef first with search_parties.

An officer can hold several per-registrar profiles, so the result is person-level (KubeRef, Name, Active)
plus a `Profiles` array — one entry per registrar profile. Each profile carries: Registrar, Country,
Jurisdiction, Type (Individual/Corporate), Status, IdentifierCode, AccessCategories, DateOfBirth,
DateOfDeath, CountryOfBirth, Gender, Ethnicity, Nationality, CountryOfResidence, ResidentialAddress,
CorrespondenceAddress, EmailAddress, ContactPhoneNumber, NiSsNumber, Occupation,
ConfidentialResidentialAddress.

Other parts of an officer's record have their own tools: get_officer_appointments (the entities they are
appointed to), get_officer_roles (entity-level service-role appointments such as auditor),
get_officer_alternates (appointments held as an alternate), get_officer_external_appointments
(appointments at companies outside this Kube instance), get_officer_committees (committees sat on),
get_officer_contacts (contact records), get_officer_addresses (address book) and get_officer_udfs (user
defined field values).

Withheld vs not-recorded: a field is null/absent either because no value is recorded, or because it was
withheld. Each profile's `RedactedProperties` lists the names of the fields that were withheld — each may
well hold a value, for any of several reasons this connector does not report and you should not guess at,
so do not tell the user they lack a permission. A null field NOT listed there simply has no recorded value.

tools.name: get_officer_appointments
tools.description:
List an officer's appointments (the entities they are appointed to) — Officer > Officer interests >
Appointments. Read-only and filtered to what the signed-in user may see.

Per appointment: EntityKubeRef (E| — the linked entity, follow up with get_entity), IsEntityAccessible,
OfficerKubeRef (O| — this officer), OfficerAppointmentId (stable appointment id), EntityName (the appointed-to
entity's name), RegistrarForAppointments, EntityNumber, RegistrarStatus, Name (the appointee),
AppointmentType, IsDirector (semantic directorship flag — filter on this, not the type name),
AppointedOn, ResignedOn,
AppointmentGrouping, IdentifierCode, CorrespondenceAddress, ResidentialAddress, Nationality, Occupation,
CountryOfResidency, DirectorshipType, DirectorshipStarted, DirectorshipLastRenewed, Notes.

A row may reference an entity you cannot open. It is still listed, matching how Kube shows that entity as
plain text rather than a link: the row keeps its EntityName but has NO EntityKubeRef, carries
IsEntityAccessible: false, and names EntityKubeRef, EntityNumber, RegistrarStatus and RegistrarForAppointments
— all four nulled — in its RedactedProperties. Such a row cannot be followed up with get_entity, and
this tool returns nothing else about that entity. Every other column describes this officer's own appointment
and is kept — but the per-column field permissions resolve against the appointed entity as well as this
officer, so on such a row the appointment's personal columns are commonly withheld too and named in the same
RedactedProperties. EntityName, AppointmentType, IsDirector, OfficerKubeRef and OfficerAppointmentId carry no

Read-only and filtered to what the signed-in user may see.

there is no fixed set. NEVER assume a particular field exists or guess what one means from its name — read

A field that is absent from these rows may mean any of several things, and this tool CANNOT tell them apart:

lack the grant for that field's scope. So report an absent field as "not recorded, or not visible to you" —
never state that the officer has no such field.

Three scopes, matching Kube's three inner tabs:
- `Field` — a standalone field. One row.
- `Group` — a field inside a named group of related fields. One row per field, each carrying `Group`.
- `List` — a table. One row per CELL, each carrying `List`, the 0-based `Row` number and the column's `Name`.

  reassemble a table row: `Row` restarts at 0 in every list, so grouping on `Row` alone merges cells that
  belong to different lists. List names are not guaranteed unique either.

Per row: Scope, Group, List, Row, Name (the configured field name), Value (the value as text, dates ISO
yyyy-MM-dd), DataType (the configured value type, e.g. Text, MultilineText, Date, Boolean, Integer,

silently ignored.

true) hides those, matching the ticked active-only checkbox on the Field and Group tabs. List cells are never
hidden by it, because the List tab has no such checkbox.

blanket description would be wrong for two of the three:
- `Field` — the field's own Name and Description. Does NOT match the recorded value.
- `Group` — the containing GROUP's Name and Description only. Does NOT match the member field's own Name, and
  does NOT match the recorded value.
- `List` — nothing. The List tab's box searches only the cell's rendered value, which cannot be matched
  server-side, so a List-scope row never matches a non-empty `query` — page the rows and read them instead.
AND across whitespace tokens, substring, case-insensitive, within whichever of the above a row's scope allows.

  activity can hang off an officer or an external party, and PartyType says which
  ('Entity', 'Registration', 'Officer', 'Corporate Officer', 'External Party Individual',
  'External Party Entity'). PartyKubeRef is prefixed: E| takes straight to the entity tools, O| to the
  officer tools, P| identifies an external party (no tool reads those yet).
- TeamName ('Team') and ResponsibleOwnerName ('Owner'), with ResponsibleOwnerIsCaller — whether that owner
  is the signed-in user, because a list mixing their own work with their teams' must say which rows are
  which.
- DueOn ('Due on') and IsComplete ('Complete').
- PeriodStart and PeriodEnd — the period the activity covers; for a confirmation statement PeriodEnd is
  the 'made up to' date.
- EntityName and EntityKubeRef — the company the row belongs to, which is what makes a cross-entity
  list readable and actionable, and the same as the party for an entity activity. Absent in one case:
  an activity whose FIRST party is an officer or external party, where PartyName is the answer instead.

Confirmation-statement rows also carry Cs01Eligibility { Eligible, ReasonCodes } — whether KAIA could
complete that activity for this user, without the registrar checks, which run only when a completion is
actually attempted. Do not present ReasonCodes verbatim; they are for the guided completion flow.

Open activities only by default; pass includeCompleted = true to see completed ones as well. That default is
the Activities page's own active-only gate, so TotalItems counts open activities only and is NOT how many
activities the user has — either say the count is of open work, or re-query with includeCompleted = true.

The filter parameters match the Activities page's own filter dropdowns. Prefer them over paging through
everything and filtering yourself. Every one is optional; supplying several AND-s them together.
- team, party, activityCategory, activityType, jurisdiction and filingReference take one or more SUBSTRING
  values, case-insensitive, and the values within one filter OR together ("my Filing OR Compliance
  activities"). A short value can match more than intended: read the values off returned rows to narrow a
  filter that matches too much.
- status takes one or more of 'Open', 'Overdue' or 'Complete' (case-insensitive), OR'd together — the same
  three the page's Status column and its dashboard cards use. Anything else is an error naming the three, not
  an empty page. An activity is Complete when it is completed, otherwise Overdue when its due date has
  passed, otherwise Open.
- isOverdue / isOpen / isComplete are the page's separate yes/no filters for those same three states.
  isComplete means what it does on get_entity_activities. They AND with includeCompleted, so asking for
  completed work needs includeCompleted = true as well — otherwise the open-only default has already
  excluded every row isComplete = true could match.
- The date filters come in inclusive from/to pairs, applied to the date the name says: startOnOrAfter /
  startOnOrBefore (period start), endOnOrAfter / endOnOrBefore (period end), dueOnOrAfter /
  dueOnOrBefore, reminderOnOrAfter / reminderOnOrBefore, and filingPreparedOnOrAfter /
  filingPreparedOnOrBefore and filingSubmittedOnOrAfter / filingSubmittedOnOrBefore for a filing's
  prepared and submitted dates. Send one for an open-ended bound or both for a window.
  These are DATES, not date-times — send 'YYYY-MM-DD'. The whole of a bounding day is included at both ends,
  so the window is never narrower than the dates you asked for, and an activity with no date recorded in
  that column is excluded by either bound.
- party and jurisdiction read the same consolidated party record the page's columns do, so an activity
  with no party recorded is excluded by either.

Paged: Items plus Page, PageSize, TotalItems.

Paged: `Items` is one page; `TotalItems` is the total match count.
A pure count ("how many …") needs only `TotalItems` from page 1.
For the complete set (summary, aggregate, comparison, anything over "all"), page with `pageSize` 100 (the max), incrementing `page`, until you have all `TotalItems` items BEFORE answering — one page is not a sufficient basis.
When `TotalItems` is large, prefer narrowing with the filter parameters; page everything only when the complete set is genuinely required.

kubeRef.description: Entity KubeRef, E|-prefixed (e.g. 'E|6FE4BF'). Omit to search every entity the user can see.

activityType.description: Activity-type name (substring, case-insensitive; e.g. 'Confirmation statement'); any one matches. Omit for all types.

includeCompleted.description: true to include completed activities as well; default false (open activities only), matching the active-only gate the Activities page applies. This is that gate, NOT the Complete filter: `isComplete`, `isOpen` and `status` AND with it, so asking for completed work needs includeCompleted = true as well.

pageSize.description: Default 25, max 100. Use 100 when retrieving the full result set.

team.description: Team name (substring, case-insensitive); any one matches. Omit for all teams.

party.description: Party name (substring, case-insensitive) — the Party column, usually the entity. Any one matches; omit for all parties.

activityCategory.description: Activity-category name (substring, case-insensitive; e.g. 'Filing'); any one matches. Omit for all categories.

jurisdiction.description: Jurisdiction name (substring, case-insensitive; e.g. 'England and Wales'); any one matches. Omit for all jurisdictions.

status.description: Activity status: 'Open', 'Overdue' or 'Complete'; any one matches. Omit for all statuses.

filingReference.description: Filing reference (substring, case-insensitive); any one matches. Omit for all filings.

startOnOrAfter.description: Earliest period start, inclusive; omit for no lower bound.

startOnOrBefore.description: Latest period start, inclusive; omit for no upper bound.

endOnOrAfter.description: Earliest period end, inclusive; omit for no lower bound.

endOnOrBefore.description: Latest period end, inclusive; omit for no upper bound.

dueOnOrAfter.description: Earliest due date, inclusive; omit for no lower bound.

dueOnOrBefore.description: Latest due date, inclusive; omit for no upper bound.

reminderOnOrAfter.description: Earliest reminder date, inclusive; omit for no lower bound.

reminderOnOrBefore.description: Latest reminder date, inclusive; omit for no upper bound.

filingPreparedOnOrAfter.description: Earliest filing prepared date, inclusive; omit for no lower bound.

filingPreparedOnOrBefore.description: Latest filing prepared date, inclusive; omit for no upper bound.

filingSubmittedOnOrAfter.description: Earliest filing submitted date, inclusive; omit for no lower bound.

filingSubmittedOnOrBefore.description: Latest filing submitted date, inclusive; omit for no upper bound.

isOverdue.description: true = overdue only (past due and not completed), false = everything else. Omit to not filter on being overdue.

isOpen.description: true = open only (not completed), false = completed only. Omit to not filter on being open.

isComplete.description: true = completed only, false = outstanding only. Omit to not filter on completion. Same meaning as isComplete on get_entity_activities. AND-ed with includeCompleted, so completed activities need includeCompleted = true as well.
